summary: Phalerus or Phalereus (Ancient Greek: Φάληρος / Φαληρεύς) was an Athenian Argonaut, son of Alcon. Apollonius, Hyginus, and the Orphic Argonautica place him among Jason's crew; Pausanias connects the Attic harbour of Phaleron with his name and memory.

sections.heading: Argonaut from Attica
paragraphs: Apollonius of Rhodes numbers Phalerus son of Alcon among the Athenians who sailed with Jason. Hyginus and the Argonautica Orphica repeat the Attic Argonaut. Tradition held that Alcon once shot a snake that threatened the boy's life — a parental exploit that frames the son's later voyage.
Pausanias, describing the road from Athens to the sea, treats Phalerus as the eponym remembered at the harbour of Phaleron, tying the Argonaut to the coastal deme that bore his name.

sections.heading: Homonyms
paragraphs: This atlas entry (phalerus-athens) is the Athenian Argonaut. Other Phalerus/Phalereus figures include a Lapith who fought in the Centauromachy at Pirithous' wedding, a Spartan son of Icarius and Asterodia (brother of Penelope in one stemma), and a Trojan warrior slain by Neoptolemus in Quintus of Smyrna.
